How have Iranian women shaped their place in Iranian society since the 1979 Islamic Revolution, and why does Dr. Shirin Saeidi believe their experiences are often misrepresented? In an interview with Al Mayadeen English's Rasha Reslan, Iranian-American political scientist and Middle East studies scholar Dr. Shirin Saeidi discusses her book Women and the Islamic Republic, challenging dominant Western narratives about Iranian women and their relationship with the government. She explains her concept of "activist citizenship," argues that women's rights have been used to justify foreign intervention against Iran, and examines the role Iranian women play in shaping their country's political and social life. Dr. Saeidi also discusses the end of her university employment after her public positions on Palestine and Iran, the backlash against her scholarship, and the international attention her story has received: "My voice became a threat to them." Watch the full interview as Dr. Saeidi addresses her critics, reflects on academic freedom, and explains why she believes foreign intervention cannot determine Iran's future: https://youtu.be/4-tGkhpkLMs
